what_this_is: Automated evidence for the viewer picture break prototype. It is software evidence from Jest in a fresh worktree, not a Vega build, a native observation or a user study.

environment.machine: the project Mac, isolated git worktree
environment.install: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund in app/, 1643 packages in 11 s; no node_modules or generated output copied from another checkout

full_app_suite.existing_tests_reference: results/native-checkpoint-2026-10-14/outer-only-full-tests.txt records 1198 passed and 4 skipped on e51529c before this change

existing_player_suites_before_change.command: npx jest --runInBand --watchman=false --coverage=false test/calmframes/playbackUi.test.tsx test/screens/PlayerScreen.test.tsx test/screens/playerWiring.test.tsx test/calmframes/skipOwnsOk.test.tsx test/calmframes/uiCapture.test.tsx test/calmframes/tenFoot.test.tsx test/screens/hideLog.test.tsx

seen_to_fail.how: Each line broke one rule or one player hookup on purpose, ran the picture break suites, then restored the file and confirmed it byte identical with cmp.

results.broken: the break replaces the schedule instead of adding to it
no OK grace after a return
player controls keep OK during a break
scene still shown during a break
the player ignores the break's cover
the break records a frame the app flash check never analyzed

defects_found_while_building: A second OK press right after the picture returned reached the player controls and paused the film. Fixed with a one second grace in which OK stays with the break (M5 and P1 guard it).

The first property generator used the wrong segment field names behind an unchecked cast, so every generated schedule was empty and the schedule properties passed without testing anything. Fixed with the real type; the tests now assert that schedules are non-empty and that returns were held back by holds in many runs.

The shared playback harness's remote() calls whichever key listener registered last. After a state change in the player screen that was the screen's own listener, not the controls'. No existing test calls remote(); the new tests deliver each press to every current listener in one dispatch.
After rebasing onto e51529c, the first integration test assumed captions start on; it failed against d52d657 and was rewritten before the implementation was recommitted.
not_run_here: Vega build, install and native observation: the simulator and native builds belong to the Codex native task.
tools/ui_flashmap.mjs: the break draws no new frame; a test asserts it records only frames already in ALL_UI_FRAMES.
The adult walkthrough in docs/WORKING_BACKWARDS.md section 5: unperformed, so comprehension and preference are unknown.
base_note: The work began on 60eca59 and was rebased onto e51529c, the native branch head at handoff, before anything was pushed. Every check below ran on the rebased tree.
adapted_to_native_changes: d52d657 starts Harbor's captions Off. The integration tests now turn English captions on before a break in one case and keep the Off default in another; the break keeps whichever choice the viewer made.
0090551 lets the seekbar yield preferred focus when the controls do not own OK. The break sets that ownership, so it benefits once the seekbar finding below is fixed.

finding_for_codex.summary: Seekbar's React.memo comparison ignores the new hasTVPreferredFocus prop, so the value only changes when the seekbar remounts. A countdown card or a picture break that appears while the controls are mounted leaves the seekbar claiming preferred focus.
finding_for_codex.reproduction: results/seekbar_focus_repro_2026-10-13/seekbarFocusRepro.test.tsx.txt (copy into app/test/calmframes/ as a .tsx file to run)
finding_for_codex.proposed_fix: results/seekbar_focus_repro_2026-10-13/proposed-fix.patch, one line added to the comparison
finding_for_codex.not_applied_here: Seekbar.tsx belongs to the Codex native task; this branch leaves it unchanged.
